title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to evaluate whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline improves oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes) with model_calls_used=200 and repair_calls_invoked=0. Results: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. The null outcome is design‑bound: a single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every task, so the repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for follow‑ups that avoid the ceiling effect (independent generation semantics; calibrated difficulty; larger repair budgets).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs show promise for intent→configuration NetOps automation, but model outputs can be plausibly executable yet operationally incorrect. A common mitigation architecture pairs generation with deterministic validators and repair (generate→validate→repair). We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to confirm whether a verifier‑assisted pipeline increases oracle pass rates relative to unconstrained generation under a tightly specified, auditable workflow. Key frozen design choices (preregistration SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7...) included: a paired design (Npairs=200), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring records, manifests and per‑file SHA‑256 digests were archived (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce92558ed... and execution/execution_manifest.json listing). This paper reports the artifact‑anchored run, the exact confirmatory inference, deterministic reconciliation, and concrete reproducible recommendations for informative follow‑ups.
sections.related_work: Prior work has explored LLM‑based intent translation, constraint‑guided generation, and verifier‑grounded repair (examples in the supplied evidence bundle include MeshAgent; NetConfEval; verifier‑grounded program repair methods such as StruSpec). Those studies motivate verifier assistance but often differ in generation semantics, task difficulty, and artifact transparency. Our contribution is methodological: a fully preregistered, archived, reproducible paired test with deterministic reconciliation of all artifacts and per‑file SHA‑256 digests so that the precise causal role of design choices (notably shared_initial_candidate semantics) can be audited.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan: We froze the estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), sample (200 paired tasks stratified by protocol and vendor), generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), model (gpt‑5‑mini via adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), repair budget (≤1), analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1: paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and stopping rules. The full preregistration is archived and hashed (SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7...). Task bank and stratification: the preregistered task manifest contains 200 pairs (protocol buckets: BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 each) with vendor allocation per protocol Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (total Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64) and complexity split simple=100 / complex=100 (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Generation and execution semantics: shared_initial_candidate means one generator call per pair; that single generated candidate was provided verbatim to both baseline (unconstrained) and guarded (verifier‑assisted) scorers. Every provider call, raw response, and provider trace is archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ and hashed (examples: execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt). Validator, scoring, and repair: the validator returns normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, final_state, validity boolean, and violation list; repair was permitted but in this run never applied (repair_applied=false in scoring artifacts). Analysis pipeline: the registered analysis executor read per‑pair scoring JSONs and produced condition_summary and paired_contingency artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 1cb072b4...; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...). Deterministic reconciliation verified accounting across provider calls, raw outputs, and scoring (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
sections.results: Execution outcomes (artifact‑backed): The run completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per pair), repair_calls_invoked=0. Scoring summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 1cb072b4...): baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100.0%); guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100.0%). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...): n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory inference (analysis/results.json; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 940b48e7...): paired estimate = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Representative scoring artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) show validator detail: parsed_command_count, final_state, normalized_configuration and repair_applied=false. Deterministic reconciliation confirms consistency across all archived artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 799b23b9...).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and causal diagnosis: The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one generated candidate per pair that both conditions consumed; because every shared candidate passed the deterministic validator, the repair stage never ran (repair_calls_invoked=0). Thus the observed null difference is a direct consequence of the frozen generation semantics and the empirical fact that the chosen generator produced globally passing candidates for the provided task bank. The run therefore answers the preregistered estimand exactly under the frozen design but does not evaluate repair effectiveness in scenarios where baseline candidates fail. Statistical consequences of the degenerate contingency: perfect concordance (n11=200) yields zero empirical variance for the paired difference and a degenerate bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; this is the correct inferential outcome for the observed data and preregistered analysis executor (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Practical recommendations grounded in the archive: the artifact bundle and manifests permit exact replication and two immediate, low‑risk preregistered variants that enable repair exercise and informative contrasts: (1) independent generation semantics (one generator call per condition per pair) — expected to consume ≈400 generator calls and permit repairs to act when baseline candidates fail; (2) increase task difficulty or adversarialize a subset of tasks in the manifest so that some initial candidates fail the validator (the existing manifest entries include difficulty labels and required_sequence fields to support reproducible difficulty calibration). Other reproducible extensions (all supported by the archived artifacts) include increasing the repair budget (>1), enabling iterative repair loops, and running multi‑model replications across different generator identifiers. Reproducibility note: every required artifact and per‑file SHA‑256 digest is archived (execution/execution_manifest.json lists file hashes), enabling independent auditors to rerun or extend the experiment deterministically.
sections.conclusion: Under the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, Npairs=200, repair budget ≤1), the verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline produced no measurable improvement: both baseline and guarded conditions achieved 200/200 oracle passes and the paired difference is 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.00). The null outcome is design‑bound: the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every task, so repair was never invoked. We publish the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests) and recommend preregistered follow‑ups (independent generation semantics and calibrated task difficulty) that are directly reproducible from the provided artifacts and that will permit a valid measurement of repair efficacy.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact‑backed):
- Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). This master prompt launched the autonomous post‑lock research run. The Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) prior to the autonomy lock; all substantive research actions reported here were performed autonomously after the lock.
- Preregistration (frozen): study id = study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze the estimand, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, validator, repair budget, sampling plan, stopping rules, and analysis executor.
- Declared LLM and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Provider call traces and raw responses archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair and identical candidate consumed by both baseline and guarded conditions). This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=200 (artifact: execution/execution_manifest.json) and directly resulted in repair not being exercised (repair_calls_invoked=0; repair_applied=false in execution/scoring/* artifacts).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate and produced validator traces (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c3...). The validator enforces emulation‑based constraints (sequence, reachability, protected interfaces); all scoring records are archived and hashed.
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this execution repair calls were never invoked (artifact evidence in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Analysis procedures (frozen and executed): paired_binary_analysis_v1 (paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 1cb072b4...), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 940b48e7...).
- Execution and reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring record, manifest and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic reconciliation confirms accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 799b23b9...). All artifact paths and hashes cited above are present in the supplied artifact bundle for independent audit and deterministic rerun.
- Human involvement: pre‑lock collaborative development and topic selection by the Research Director. No human performed manual substantive edits to the manuscript text after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; model identifier did not change mid‑run; no pairs were excluded. The repair stage was not triggered because shared initial candidates passed the deterministic validator for every pair. Full execution manifest (per‑file SHA‑256 list) documents all raw and processed artifacts.
limitations: Confirmatory findings apply only to the exact preregistered configuration (shared_initial_candidate semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, Npairs=200).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics created a ceiling effect: one shared generator call per pair passed the oracle in all pairs, so repair was never exercised (repair_calls_invoked=0), preventing measurement of repair efficacy in this run.
Emulation and a deterministic validator do not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor device nondeterminism, firmware differences, runtime failures).
Single declared model limits generalization to other model families and instruction‑tuning regimes.
Repair budget was intentionally constrained (≤1 call/task); iterative or larger budgets remain unexplored in this execution.
Oracle blind spots remain possible; validator coverage diagnostics are archived per pair and annotated in scoring artifacts.
